pr_title: xtensa: check for valid stack pointers before dumping stack and printing backtraces
pr_body:
During exception, to get information on the interrupted context (PC, PS, EXCCAUSE, etc.) requires de-referencing pointers (e.g. `frame->ptr_to_bsa` then `bsa->pc`). If the stack is corrupted, it could lead to infinite exceptions. So better check them.

(See individual commits for more details.)

Fixes #74433
pr_comments:
> The first patch creeps me out a bit, can we at least file a bug on that? Almost certainly that's a symptom of something bad. Regarding the bigger change: is this really that useful? Exception entry isn't safe on xtensa right now and can't easily be made so (yes, still need to get call0 in). Stack corruption is just as likely to lead to an explosion on interrupt entry that this can't fix, no? Why spend code bytes to handle this particular subset of failures?

This, to certain extent, prevents infinite faulting due to stack corruption of the frame pointer, especially `frame->ptr_to_bsa` being bad. Another big part is to prevent backtrace from going through bad pointers. The sure way to trigger this is via `tests/kernel/mem_protect/stackprot` with `qemu_xtensa/dc233c/mmu`. The `alt_thread` is definitely corrupting the stack frame and the BSA pointer.

issue_context.title: xtensa: unwinding stack during exception can access invalid memory
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Sometimes when unwinding stack on Xtensa during exception, especially with a corrupted stack, it can access invalid memory.

**Expected behavior**
Do not access invalid memory.

**Impact**
Annoyance for now as it is currently a rare occurrence.

review_comments: Can we please root cause this instead of merging the workaround?  That sounds like stack overflow of the interrupt frame or something equally terrifying.  Does it happen in emulation anywhere?

Stack frame was definitely corrupted when this happened, and the corruption was deliberate. Though I have no idea why it would print `(null)` instead of nothing (via `%s`). Debugging via GDB always makes it work again.
